title: C10: restrict model write permissions via acceptEdits + settings file
goal: Replace --dangerously-skip-permissions at both route.sh spawn sites with --permission-mode acceptEdits plus a jq-validated settings file that grants only the worktree and stage scratch dir, and amend ADR-018 to record the change.

steps.description: Verify core/router/permissions.sh is complete: exports _zbuild_build_permissions_settings (writes ${ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH:-$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)}/claude-settings.json with allowedDirectories=[ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT, ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH], validates with jq, sets _ZBUILD_PERMISSIONS_SETTINGS_FILE, returns rc=1 on failure) and _zbuild_permission_args (emits --permission-mode acceptEdits --settings <file>). File already exists in worktree; confirm it matches spec and needs no edits.

Verify core/router/route.sh wiring: source block at ~line 101-105 conditionally sources permissions.sh; single-shot path at ~line 814-816 calls _zbuild_build_permissions_settings (abort on rc!=0) then appends _zbuild_permission_args output to _claude_args; agent-loop path at ~line 1572-1574 does the same. Confirm no --dangerously-skip-permissions remains in any non-comment line. SPEC-1 and SPEC-4 satisfied. File already committed; verify correctness only.

Verify tests/unit/router-permissions-test.sh covers SPEC-2 (settings file allowedDirectories equals ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT and ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH), SPEC-3 (jq absent or broken causes _zbuild_build_permissions_settings to return rc!=0, not silently bypass), SPEC-4 (grep core/router/ for non-comment dangerously-skip-permissions returns empty). File already exists; confirm all three SPECs are covered and assertions use project test-helpers style.

Verify tests/unit/router-claude-flags-test.sh lines 86-132 replace --dangerously-skip-permissions assertions with assert_contains for --permission-mode and acceptEdits tokens for both T1 (single-shot) and T2 (JSON-mode) test cases. Confirm --settings token also asserted. Preserve order-insensitive token-set style matching :73-77.

Verify tests/integration/router-claude-flags-test.sh line ~118-127 replaces --dangerously-skip-permissions assertion with --permission-mode and acceptEdits assertions. Confirm --settings token also asserted in e2e argv check.

Update docs/adr/ADR-018-stage-invocation-modes.md: the Amended block at lines 9-16 already supersedes lines 25,28-33,40,41,68,350,462. Additionally update line 81 (Pattern 1 current behavior description) to replace '--dangerously-skip-permissions' with '--permission-mode acceptEdits --settings <file>' and add note that bypassPermissions is the renamed equivalent and must not be used. Update Decision point 1 at line 363 to note the flag was amended by #1919. These changes make the body consistent with the amendment block and prevent the body from contradicting current behavior.

notes: Most implementation is already committed on this branch (ded102e, 71a2d59): permissions.sh, route.sh wiring, all three test files. The build stage should verify those files match spec, then focus on the ADR-018 body updates in step-6 which remain incomplete (the Amended block exists but body line 81 still says --dangerously-skip-permissions in the Pattern 1 current-behavior description). P0-P4 probe results are a human prerequisite recorded in the issue, not a code deliverable. grep -rn 'skip-permissions' docs/wiki/ already returns clean. tests/unit/stage-checkpoint-test.sh:259-271 greps route.sh for _claude_args array rewrite and turn-cap lines well away from the changed sites and should pass unchanged. Paths in permissions.sh derive from ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT and ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH env vars (ADR-058 §1), not literals, satisfying the ADR-059 layout-move requirement. The settings file is written to ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH (a C8-sanctioned area), satisfying redaction-chokepoint-test.sh:47,66-70 which constrains settings writes to core/router/. SPEC-4 grep in router-permissions-test.sh excludes comment lines (grep -v '^[^:]*:[0-9]*:[[:space:]]*#') so comment-only references in permissions.sh and route.sh do not trigger false failures.
